info.title: AFR.IM API
info.description: Public, key-free read API for the AFR.IM AI-Friendliness Rating (AFR) directory. All JSON endpoints send Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *. Ratings are snapshots computed from public, reproducible evidence — see GET /api/v1/method for the machine-readable standard.

post.summary: Request a scan of a site
post.description: Fully automatic inclusion. Registered domains only (eTLD+1 heuristic): subdomains like blog.example.com are rejected with error subdomain_not_allowed, www is stripped. Already-listed domains return status 'exists' (open the detail page); already-queued domains return status 'queued' (idempotent, no quota burned). New submissions are queued AND immediately dispatch the scan workflow, so a typical listing is searchable within ~10 minutes (etaSeconds covers scan + rebuild); if dispatch is deferred the next daily scan (02:00 UTC) collects it. Rate-limited to 5 new submissions per IP per day. New entries carry etaSeconds 600 (scan plus rebuild) and dispatch 'scheduled' | 'ok' | 'deferred'; the idempotent 'exists'/'queued' responses omit dispatch. The request is gated by a human check: the body field 'turnstile_token' carries a Cloudflare Turnstile token minted by the widget on the AFR submit form (action 'afr_submit'). Without a valid token the endpoint answers 400 { "error": "turnstile_failed", "reason": "missing_token" | "invalid_token" | "wrong_action" | "verify_failed" } and nothing is queued. AI agents and scripts that cannot run a browser widget may send the 'X-AFR-Agent-Key' request header instead: a key issued by AFR and not revoked skips the human check (self-service issuance is not open yet).

parameters.name: X-AFR-Agent-Key
parameters.description: Agent key issued by AFR. When present and valid — the key's SHA-256 hash is in the api_keys table and not revoked — the human check is skipped and turnstile_token is not required. Self-service issuance is not open yet: ask AFR for a key.

domain.description: Bare registered domain, e.g. example.com (subdomains rejected)

turnstile_token.description: Human-verification token: a Cloudflare Turnstile token (action 'afr_submit') minted by the widget on the AFR submit form. Optional in the schema, required in practice — a request without a valid token is answered 400 turnstile_failed — unless the caller sends a valid 'X-AFR-Agent-Key' header, which skips the human check.

post.summary: Request an on-demand scan of a domain
post.description: Interactive-session variant of a submission: looser quota tiers (10 per IP per day, 1 per domain per 30-minute window, 50 globally per day). Already-listed domains return status 'exists' and already-queued domains return status 'queued' with no quota burned - both omit the dispatch field. The scan workflow is dispatched in the background, so the response never waits for GitHub: 'scheduled' means triggered, 'deferred' means the nightly run will pick it up (still queued, not lost). The same human check as the submission endpoint applies: the body field 'turnstile_token' carries a Cloudflare Turnstile token minted by the widget on the AFR search page (action 'afr_search_scan'), and a missing or invalid token is answered 400 { "error": "turnstile_failed", "reason": "missing_token" | "invalid_token" | "wrong_action" | "verify_failed" }. AI agents and scripts that cannot run a browser widget may send the 'X-AFR-Agent-Key' request header instead: a key issued by AFR and not revoked skips the human check (self-service issuance is not open yet).

post.summary: Request a domain-control challenge for an owner mailbox
post.description: Starts the owner-mailbox registration of a domain (score-change notifications). The body carries the domain and the address that should receive the notices; AFR answers with a challenge plus the three ways to publish it on the domain (DNS TXT record, well-known file, homepage meta tag). The challenge is bound to the address, valid for 24 hours and can be spent only once. Quotas: 3 challenges per domain per day, 5 per IP per hour. A human check is part of the contract: the body must also carry { "turnstile_token": "…" } (a Cloudflare Turnstile token, action 'afr_owner_email', minted by the widget on the site detail page). A missing, expired or foreign token is answered 400 { "error": "turnstile_failed", "reason": "missing_token" | "invalid_token" | "wrong_action" | "verify_failed" } — no challenge is minted and no rate-limit budget is spent. An agent that cannot run the widget may send the 'X-AFR-Agent-Key' header instead (a key issued by AFR, not self-service yet).

get.description: Reads the mailbox of a domain. The management token of that mailbox must be sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' — without it, with a wrong token, or with the token of another domain the answer is 401 unauthorized. The address is never returned in full: only masked, e.g. 'o***@example.com'.

parameters.description: Bare registered domain, e.g. example.com

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: Bearer token of the confirmed mailbox, e.g. 'Bearer manage-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef'

200.description: The mailbox state — the address is masked

401.description: unauthorized — the management token is missing, wrong or belongs to another domain

delete.summary: Unregister the mailbox of a domain
delete.description: The owner removes the mailbox of a domain: the confirmed row is deleted, so no score-change mail is sent any more. The management token of that mailbox is the lock — without it, with a wrong token, or with the token of another domain nothing is deleted (401 unauthorized). The AFR records (score history, notification outbox) stay untouched.

get.summary: Confirm the mailbox and collect the management token
get.description: Consumes the single-use confirmation token of the mail link. On success it answers { "verified": true, "domain": "…", "manageToken": "manage-…" }. The management token is returned exactly once — only its hash is stored, so AFR can never show it again. Keep it: it authorises every later read of the mailbox and the notification switch. 400 invalid_or_expired_token, 429 rate_limited (20 verifications per IP per hour).

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The single-use confirmation token from the mail link

200.description: The mailbox is confirmed and the management token is handed out — once

400.description: invalid_or_expired_token — the token is unknown, expired or already spent

429.description: Rate limited — 20 verifications per IP per hour

post.description: Starts the recovery of a lost management token of a confirmed mailbox. None of the three locks weakens: the domain has to publish a fresh challenge (asked for at POST /api/v1/owners/email/start) and AFR has to observe it there, the reset mail goes to the confirmed address only, and the recovery link hands out a new management token and rotates the stored one — the old token stops working. The answer never carries the link or the token; they exist once, in the mail. Errors: 400 invalid_domain | invalid_email | invalid_challenge | turnstile_failed, 403 recovery_not_available (one opaque code for 'this domain has no confirmed mailbox' and 'this address is not the confirmed mailbox') | challenge_not_found | domain_control_failed (the answer carries a per-method 'checks' summary of what AFR saw on the domain), 429 rate_limited (3 recoveries per domain per day, 5 per IP per hour), 502 email_delivery_failed, 503 email_not_configured.

parameters.name: X-AFR-Agent-Key
parameters.description: Agent key issued by AFR. When present and valid — the key's SHA-256 hash is in the api_keys table and not revoked — the human check is skipped and turnstile_token is not required. Self-service issuance is not open yet: ask AFR for a key.

email.description: The confirmed address of the mailbox — the reset mail goes there and nowhere else

challenge.description: A fresh domain-control challenge, published on the domain, e.g. ch-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

turnstile_token.description: Human-verification token: a Cloudflare Turnstile token (action 'afr_owner_email') minted by the widget on the AFR site detail page. Optional in the schema, required in practice — a request without a valid token is answered 400 turnstile_failed — unless the caller sends a valid 'X-AFR-Agent-Key' header, which skips the human check.

200.description: The recovery mail was sent to the confirmed address

400.description: Invalid parameter (invalid_domain, invalid_email, invalid_challenge) or a failed human check — { "error": "turnstile_failed", "reason": "missing_token" | "invalid_token" | "wrong_action" | "verify_failed" }. Nothing is stored and no rate-limit budget is spent.

403.description: recovery_not_available (the opaque code of a refused recovery — it never says whether the domain has a mailbox or which address it uses), challenge_not_found (no unused, unexpired challenge for this domain and address) or domain_control_failed (the platform did not see the challenge on the domain; the answer then carries a 'checks' array with one entry per method).

429.description: Rate limited — 3 recoveries per domain per day, 5 per IP per hour

get.summary: Spend the recovery link and collect the new management token
get.description: Consumes the single-use recovery token of the mail link. On success it answers { "verified": true, "domain": "…", "manageToken": "manage-…" } and rotates the management token of the mailbox: the previous token stops working immediately. The link works once — replaying it is answered 400 invalid_or_expired_token. 429 rate_limited (20 verifications per IP per hour).

parameters.description: The single-use recovery token from the mail link

200.description: The recovery is done and a new management token is handed out — once

400.description: invalid_or_expired_token — the token is unknown, expired or already spent

429.description: Rate limited — 20 verifications per IP per hour

post.summary: Switch the score-change notifications on or off
post.description: Turns the score-change mails of a domain on or off. The management token of that mailbox must be sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'. 400 invalid_domain | invalid_notify, 401 unauthorized.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: Bearer token of the confirmed mailbox, e.g. 'Bearer manage-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef'

revision.description: Documentation revision; independent of engine version

dispatch.description: Scan-workflow dispatch result (new submissions only). 'scheduled' = handed to the runtime and triggered in the background (production); 'ok' = triggered and confirmed before responding; 'deferred' = trigger did not fire, the nightly run collects the entry anyway. Idempotent 'exists'/'queued' responses omit this field.
